events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Monsoonal moisture will stream northward into most of Northern and
Central Nevada today, with historically high atmospheric moisture
content. The strongest showers and thunderstorms today will produce
intense rainfall rates, resulting in the potential of flash flooding.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Most of Northern and Central Nevada.

* WHEN...From 11 AM PDT this morning until 11 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The strongest showers and thunderstorms today will produce
rainfall rates of around one and one quarter of an inch per
hour, resulting in the potential of flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

SVROKX

The National Weather Service in Upton NY has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Hudson County in northeastern New Jersey...
Eastern Passaic County in northeastern New Jersey...
Bergen County in northeastern New Jersey...
Northern Essex County in northeastern New Jersey...

* Until 1115 AM EDT.

* At 1014 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from near Ramsey to Wayne to near Fairfield, moving east

damage to trees and power lines.

* Severe thunderstorms will be near...
Paterson and Paramus around 1020 AM EDT.
Passaic and Bloomfield around 1025 AM EDT.
Hackensack and Bergenfield around 1030 AM EDT.
Lyndhurst and Tappan around 1035 AM EDT.
Secaucus and Ridgefield around 1040 AM EDT.
Union City around 1045 AM EDT.
Hoboken around 1050 AM EDT.

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 31.0 feet, The Nueces River and Turkey Creek are a
mile and a half wide south and west of Crystal City. Farm to
Market 190 is flooded over a mile near the Nueces River and the
bridge floor is flooded. Livestock should be moved from the flood
plain. Upstream, Highway 85 becomes impassable as routed water
spills into Soldier Slough and over the highway.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM CDT Tuesday the stage was 29.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 8:30 AM CDT Tuesday was 30.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 30.3
feet just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
30.2 feet on 07/04/2002.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northeast New Jersey, including the following
areas, Eastern Bergen, Eastern Essex, Eastern Passaic, Eastern
Union, Hudson, Western Bergen, Western Essex, Western Passaic and
Western Union and southeast New York, including the following
areas, Bronx, Kings (Brooklyn), New York (Manhattan), Northern
Queens, Richmond (Staten Island) and Southern Queens.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of heavy downpours and thunderstorms are
expected this morning into tonight. Averaged rainfall totals
will be between 1 and 2 inches, with localized swaths of 3 to
4 inches possible. Peak rainfall rates in the strongest
storms could be 2-3 inches per hour.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 8
to 11 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa
Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday
night. For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM this afternoon to
6 AM CDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening swimming
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
